questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I knew FGV was a reference in Latin America, and it was an amazing opportunity to become fluent in portuguese.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Covid restrictions obviously impacted my stay, but I was still satisfied with my exchange.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. FGV has a very good international office, that can help you with almost anything.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had their support with my visa situation, and they also helped a lot in presenting the city of Rio to us.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy. In Rio you can easily find short term rentals on airbnb, OLX or Zapmoveis that are easily affordable if you receive SU.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is important to know which area you live in. Rio is not the safest city in the world, so it is important to get some local tips or help from the international office. If you stay near FGV in Botafogo or Flamengo it is pretty safe.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very easy. They guide you through the add/drop week and help you register.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The first week you have a chance to take as many classes as you want to try them out. Afterwards you need to submit your final choices before the friday of the second week of classes.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The international office guides you through the entire process.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try out as many classes as you can. I ended up doing different classes than I had expected because of the professors.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It depended a lot on the course. Some of the courses in English were on undergraduate level, and at times quite easy. However, since I speak portuguese I had some Graduate level courses that were quite challenging.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I would say it is more theoretical and less practical than what we are used to at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
International contract law 
Anatomy of corporate law
Direito Transnacional
Brazilian Constitutional law
International tax law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The international contracts law class was very interesting. If you wish to learn more about Brazil, I would recommend the Constitutional law class.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: It is more expensive to buy data for your phone than in Denmark. Food prices also vary alot depending on where you shop, so try to find the cheap supermarkets.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Pandemic so many things were not active.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Normally there are parties, lectures and other cultural gatherings.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I played football at Aterro do Flamengo (a park) with some of the students from FGV. Great way to meet local friends.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go explore Rio de Janeiro state or the country of Brazil. It is the most warm and welcoming culture in the world.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Brazilians are super friendly, and even if you do not speak portuguese, they will do their outmost to help you.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Learn some basic portuguese. Most FGV students speak English, but it is still nice to be able to get by on your own. Participate in the different events they host!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Compared to Denmark, Brazil has a pretty heavy bureaucracy. Expect to stand in line a lot.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The Brazilians. It is literally the easiest place to settle in. Without much effort, you will be invited to samba parties, Caipirinha nights, beach volley matches etc etc.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Learn some basic portuguese. It helps a lot. 
Be open, go try out all the things that Brazil and the Brazilians have to offer. If you just stay in Ipanema with all the other gringos, you could have might as well stayed home in Europe. 
Stay safe. Brazil is not Denmark, and you have to take some precautions at night. Do not walk around like if you were in Copenhagen.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: None that I can think of.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The academic connections to my professors. They are all very welcoming and eager to stay in touch.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The bureaucracy first and foremost.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
